title: Absence Allowances Under Occupancy and Residency Certification Plans
content:
How long a borrower may be away before the home stops counting as the principal residence, and how a health-care absence is evidenced, dated and followed up, are fixed for the Occupancy and Residency Certification product by the figures below. They are identical under each of the six plans (Standard Annual Certification, Joint Borrower Certification, Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification, Deferral Period Certification, Living Trust Certification and Authorized Representative Certification).

## Absence figures

| Setting | Value under every plan |
|---|---|
| Longest consecutive absence for physical or mental illness before the home stops counting as the principal residence | 12 calendar months |
| Interval between contacts during a health-care absence | 90 calendar days |
| Evidence required to open health-care absence monitoring | a facility admission letter |
| Date that starts a health-care absence | the facility admission date |
| Longest absence for reasons other than illness in a 12-month period before the home stops counting as the principal residence | 183 calendar days |
| Annual certification requests replaced by absence check-ins during a health-care absence | yes |

## Two kinds of absence

The schedule distinguishes an absence **because of physical or mental illness**, measured in consecutive calendar months (limit 12), from an absence **for any other reason**, measured in calendar days within a 12-month period (limit 183). The two limits are separate settings and are never added together.

## Questions the schedule answers

- *What evidence opens health-care absence monitoring?* A facility admission letter, under every plan.
- *From which date is a health-care absence counted?* The facility admission date.
- *How often is the borrower contacted while away for care?* At an interval of 90 calendar days.
- *Does the annual certification request continue during a health-care absence?* No; under every plan it is replaced by absence check-ins.

**Hypothetical illustration (generic dates).** For an illness-related absence whose facility admission date is a hypothetical 15 March, contacts fall at 90-day intervals counted from that date, the first 90 days after 15 March.
